resources.string: Merging fake twins
Two states look like twins when they go to the same places.
The trick: a final state and a non-final one are never twins.
Which pair can you split right away? Tap it.
One of them accepts the word and the other doesn't.
Final against non-final is already different.
Then look at where each one goes with the same letter.
If one goes to a pair already split, these two split too.
Only merge what no word can tell apart.
A terminal doesn't go to the table
The top of the stack can hold two kinds of symbol.
With a nonterminal on top, the parser checks the table and swaps it for the rule.
With a terminal on top, the table stays out. It only checks against the input.
The top is plus and the input is plus. What does the parser do? Tap.
Plus is a terminal. A terminal on top never goes to the table.
It matches, pops the top and moves ahead in the input.
If the terminal on top differs from the input, it's an error right away.
The table is only for nonterminals. A terminal just gets checked.
match and move on
check the table
error
The parenthesis doesn't become a node
This sum has parentheses. They change the order of the math.
In the parse tree, each parenthesis shows up as a leaf.
In the AST they vanish. The shape of the tree already keeps the order.
Which of these become nodes in the tree? Tap all of them.
The AST keeps operations and values. A grouping sign doesn't become a node.
Times and plus become nodes. The parentheses vanish.
The plus sits under the times. That's how the AST remembers the parenthesis.
The AST keeps what the program does, not how it was written.
